articles.title: Man of Tomorrow Passed An Important Post-Production Milestone
articles.summary: Man of Tomorrow's post-production process still appears on track despite all the behind-the-scenes changes at Warner Bros. caused by the merger with Paramount. In fact, director James Gunn recently shared that Man of Tomorrow had passed an important post-production editing milestone.
body: In a visual effects-heavy film like Man of Tomorrow, there's still a lot of work to do after the assembly cut stage beyond trimming unneeded footage. While this confirmation is a fairly minor update in the grand scheme of things, it's still good to know that the movie's post-production process remains on track amid all the major shake-ups at Warner Bros. Its merger with Paramount to create Skydance is imminent, and some major leadership changes are happening as a result.

Notably, Michael De Luca and Pamela Abdy, the co-CEOs of Warner Bros. Pictures who helped convince James Gunn and Peter Safran to spearhead DC Studios, are exiting the company. Thankfully for DC fans, Gunn and Safran will remain at the company after the merger. As such, it appears Gunn will see Man of Tomorrow's production through to the end and is actively working on the movie.

Man of Tomorrow is still slated for release in theaters on July 9, 2027. The only other DC Studios movies with firm release dates are Clayface (out on Oct. 23), The Batman Part 2 (out Feb. 18, 2028), and Dynamic Duo (out Sept. 22, 2028).
points: Man of Tomorrow's post-production process still appears on track despite all the behind-the-scenes changes at Warner Bros. caused by the merger with Paramount.

articles.title: Ghost of Yotei DLC’s Best Boss Fight Stars Giant Murder Bears
articles.summary: Ghost of Yōtei: Echoes of Sekigahara, the new DLC for Sucker Punch’s popular 2025 samurai game, is out now, sending players to a new region, the Ashoro Foothills. It does well in adding new and much-needed layers to Atsu, but in between all that character work is more of the open-world exploration…
body: More bounties become available throughout the DLC’s story, which is about Atsu contending with a gang called the Vipers, villains formerly loyal to the Yōtei Six’s Snake. A few bounties are for the heads of those contending for the Snake’s now-vacant spot in the Yōtei Six. One of them includes the most hilarious boss fight in the whole game, and I barely have to unsheath my katana to beat it.

Echoes of Sekigahara explores the impact the Vipers are having on not just the people of the new region of Ashoro Foothills, but its wildlife too. As such, one of the bounties is for Umakichi the Bear Slayer, a scumbag who has several bears kept in cages. He’ll sic them on his soldiers for “training,” and the boss fight arena is littered with corpses of bears.

Umakichi is a big guy with big weapons, and he doesn’t fight fair; like so many of Yōtei ’s baddies, he’s got a gaggle of goons providing him support for the fight. Thankfully, Atsu isn’t alone either. Umakichi’s lackeys are easily cut down by Atsu, and the new heavy weapons she can use help get the job done fast.

articles.title: Tonda Ros, creator of Blue Prince, has played UFO 50 for almost 700 hours: 'I think it's easily my favourite game of the last 20 years'
articles.summary: Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex.
body: Welcome to Disk Cleanup, our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?"

Tonda Ros was first drawn to PC gaming at seven years old, after playing the action-adventure classic, Beast. "It's kind of like an open, nonlinear Sokoban that's action-based and not puzzle-based," says Ros, the creator of 2025's Blue Prince. "I think it was the next year where we had a 386 PC in the house, and that's when the floodgates opened … when I played Tank Wars and the original SimCity and Star Control."

Establishing a career as a cinematographer and visual artist, in 2016, Ros began working on Blue Prince. Inspired by games like Myst, board games like Jewels in the Attic and puzzle books like Maze: Solve the World's Most Challenging Puzzle, Blue Prince was painstakingly created across the best part of a decade. When it released last year, it quickly established itself as a modern puzzling classic.

articles.title: A Beloved Critical Role Cast Member Will Officially Miss Campaign 4 for a Long Time
articles.summary: From the moment Critical Role introduced Campaign 4 and its 13-player cast, one thing was clear: Dungeon Master Brennan Lee Mulligan wasn't pulling any punches. This became even more obvious during a pivotal moment in Campaign 4's 30th episode, "Here in the Dark."
body: After a valiant battle against the undead, Teor Pridesire (Travis Willingham) perished alongside his brother Cyd in the crypts of the Tachonis estate. Willingham didn't appear in episode 31, the final episode of the arc before Campaign 4 went on break for Age of Umbra: Sallowlands. Many fans were already hyped at the thought of Travis' new character appearing in the next arc, which debuted on Aug. 27. Then he didn't.

However, thanks to Critical Role’s talk-show, Tale Gate, hosted by Whitney Moore (who plays Tyranny in Campaign 4) and featuring several guests, we now know that Willingham’s return to the Campaign 4 cast might take much longer than fans expected.

Speaking in the Beacon-exclusive segment Night Cap, Willingham took the opportunity to answer a fan who wondered when he would next appear. “I genuinely don’t have a backup character planned yet. I also don’t have a reentry point planned yet,” Willingham explained. “I feel like if you die, you got to get punished.”

articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday Poster Highlights One Of The Film's Biggest Mysteries
articles.summary: A new poster for Avengers: Doomsday was unveiled at Comic-Con Málaga on Oct. 3. Although it reveals nothing new about the film, it spotlights three characters we still don't know much about. Right in time for Halloween, this poster has me wondering who the Latverian Witches really are.
body: The new poster for Avengers: Doomsday shows Doctor Doom at the bottom of a grand staircase, presumably in Latveria. Behind him, he's flanked by three witches, each of whom wears a different color. While people colloquially call these mysterious characters Latverian Witches, Marvel has otherwise revealed little about them.

These characters will seemingly help Doctor Doom execute his grand plan in Avengers: Doomsday, but it feels unlikely they are characters we've never met before. In fact, there are several characters who would make sense as the Latverian Witches.

One simply has to look to the magical corner of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, and a lot of sensible candidates emerge. Doctor Strange, Clea, and Scarlet Witch seem like obvious fits, especially as we don't know what they have been up to since Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness.

I could see Bruce Banner as one, since Doctor Doom kidnaps him at the end of Avengers: Endgame Encore, and Sylvie from Loki would also make sense given her connections to the collapsing multiverse. It's possible, if more unlikely, that Agatha All Along characters like Agatha Harkness, Jennifer Kale, or Death show up as Latverian Witches too.

articles.title: Silent Hill: Townfall is the first horror game to make me feel bad for using a shotgun
articles.summary: Silent Hill: Townfall is a suffocating experience, especially if you're like me and love tormenting yourself with stealth, limiting the use of any kind of weapon. I spent almost all of my first playthrough forgoing any pipe or plank, or even pistol in favour of my trusty CRTV and top-notch…
body: Every horror game fan will know the liberating power of getting your hands on a shotgun in a game where you've done nothing but cower and run from danger—finally, you get to be the danger. Turns out the horrors are trapped inside this game with you, not the other way around.

I may have embodied this a bit too much when I got my hands on the shotgun in Richard's section of Townfall. Tasked with making it to the top of a 10 story office building, you need to solve puzzles and clear the way all while fending off a new kind of Silent Hill monster: the widow.

These are bloodied creatures with shrouds of flesh covering their faces. They'll hide behind doors, under desks, or just anywhere that's a bit shadowy. They'll jump out at you, stab you with a knife, and then run off to yet another hiding place. It didn't really bother me at first, their attacks don't deal a massive amount of damage, so I just kind of decided to live and let live, for a short while at least.
points: Silent Hill: Townfall is a suffocating experience, especially if you're like me and love tormenting yourself with stealth, limiting the use of any kind of weapon.

articles.title: PlatinumGames boss hints he wants to expand Bayonetta as Stellar Blade director calls the series "indispensable"
articles.summary: PlatinumGames president Atsushi Inaba has hinted he'd like to expand the character of Bayonetta and broaden her world.
body: While he stopped short of confirming a new game, Famitsu reports that when Inaba sat down with Shift Up CEO and Stellar Blade director Kim Hyung-tae during Tokyo Game Show held to mark a crossover bringing four Bayonetta-themed costumes to Stellar Blade Complete Edition on Switch 2 this November, he admitted he still had a desire to expand the franchise further.

Kim used the opportunity to gush about the series himself, calling Bayonetta "an indispensable work in my life" (albeit via machine-translation) and naming it one of his three favourite games, while admitting he had to control himself while designing his own Bayonetta-inspired "Black Dress" costume so it wouldn't go too far. He even asked, half-joking, to design characters for the next entry himself.
Asked directly about that next entry, Inaba declined to give specifics, telling Famitsu only to wait and see.

It's certainly more optimistic than recent conversations - series creator Hideki Kamiya left Platinum in October 2023, saying at the time he'd envisioned Bayonetta as a nine-part saga he may now take "to the grave" with him - and Bayonetta 3 director Yusuke Miyata has also since departed.
points: PlatinumGames president Atsushi Inaba has hinted he'd like to expand the character of Bayonetta and broaden her world.

articles.title: Yet another free fan level pack for Quake has arrived, and this one's all about a feature rarely seen in id Software's classic shooter
articles.summary: 2026 has been a truly astonishing year for Quake mapping, with both fans and professional game developers delivering some incredible death arenas for id Software's 1996 FPS.
body: You'd think the Quake community would be out of ideas by this point, but if anything, the Quake community is only growing bolder. On Friday, the community released one of its most ambitious map packs yet—a level design extravaganza all about rooftops.

Quake Rooftops Jam adds 19 custom maps to id's shooter, all riffing on the theme of the part of your house that stops the rain falling in. While rooftops might not seem like the most exciting subject for a mapping jam, it is fascinating in the context of Quake. As a corridor shooter, rooftops are rarely glimpsed in Quake. Skittering across a virtual skyline is more the domain of games like Thief: The Dark Project and its spiritual successor Dishonored.

articles.title: Nivalis Nights dares to ask what if Cyberpunk 2077 met Dave the Diver and Stardew Valley? And for now at least I'm loving the answer
articles.summary: As I throw open the windows on my first day in Nivalis, breathing in the city's neon-streaked air and watching the smog roil across the blackened sky, my government-mandated AI automata informs me the district is in lockdown and a serial killer's on the loose.
body: It is, though, kind of fascinating as it starts from a familiar point and begins building outward. It's also, for context, the follow-up to developer Ion Lands' enjoyable neo-noir delivery adventure Cloudpunk, taking that game's stylish dystopia and reimagining it as the setting for a sort of mash-up of Cyberpunk 2077, Stardew Valley, and Dave the Diver. It's an odd mix, certainly, but it works.

A lot of its early success is down to Nivalis itself. Cloudpunk's city was mostly designed to be viewed from afar, but Nivalis Nights plays out in first-person, demanding a world that can withstand closer scrutiny. And Ion Lands more than rises to the challenge. This Nivalis might still be a world built from jagged pixel-art edges, but it's a richly detailed, wonderfully evocative one (stubbornly wonky framerate aside); a chance to live your own little Blade Runner life, right down to the Vangelis-inspired soundtrack.

articles.title: RuneScape Reignited launches 2 December
articles.summary: Jagex is offering long-time, lapsed, and new RuneScape players a clean slate with RuneScape Reignited.
body: Announced at the same RuneFest 2026 event where Jagex revealed its fourth RuneScape MMO built in Unreal Engine, RuneScape Reignited is a new permanent character type launching on 2 December.

Jagex outlined the details in a blog post entitled "RuneScape As It Was Always Meant To Be", explaining how Reignited characters come with a brand-new economy and hiscores with no paid progression available.

"It plays out in the same worlds that all existing characters are already playing in, and all Reignited characters will have free access to members' content for the first 10 days following its launch," Jagex explained.

"If you've ever felt lost or left behind in RuneScape, or have been unsure of how to come back or where to begin... There genuinely has never been a better time to jump back in or to experience the full adventure from the start – so we've made a reason to do just that," the team wrote.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 features 'detailed decapitation' and 'frequent and prominent' drug use, according to hastily deleted PEGI rating
articles.summary: Age ratings for Grand Theft Auto 6 have begun rolling in, and unsurprisingly it's a game built for grown-ups, receiving both a Mature rating in the US and an 18+ rating by the ESRB.
body: As spotted by GamesRadar+, PEGI's rating (which has now been deleted from the organisation's website) stated that Grand Theft Auto 6 "features strong graphic violence, strong sexual themes, and use of illegal drugs". In and of itself, this isn't revelatory—although Grand Theft Auto doesn't tend to be especially sexual (unless you count Trevor's startling re-introduction in Grand Theft Auto 5 ).

But it's the details supplied by PEGI in each of these areas that are of greater interest. On the violence front, PEGI stated that "Violence is bloody with a high degree of realism, with certain weapons being able to cause greater damage such as detailed decapitation and dismemberment." That's a significant change from previous GTAs, where violence was mostly blood-pools, bullet-wound decals, and enemies flopping over in physics-driven animations.

articles.title: The Sunday Papers
articles.summary: Sundays are for having the first lie-in in a month. No trips to visit family, no waking in unfamiliar beds, and, best of all, no having to wait until the hosts are up before you can get started on breakfast.
body: Once that's all polished away, I will return to bed with a fresh cup of coffee and peruse the week's best writing at my own leisure.
What's that? You want me to share? Fine. You can have a read of them when I'm done.

Papers, Please is a game that emerged from the time developer Lucas Pope spent in immigration queues while travelling in Asia and the US. Every interaction with a border officer becomes an exercise in defining yourself, verifying yourself, and proving your existence is recognised. It's an experience many us may be able to relate to, but in an essay for Deleted Saves Micaela Deitz finds a new poignancy to the game.

articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday Poster Highlights Doctor Doom and 3 Latverian Witches
articles.summary: Marvel Studios has revealed a new Avengers: Doomsday poster, giving audiences a closer look not only at Doctor Doom but also at the three Latverian witches who will accompany him this December.
body: This latest look at the new Marvel Cinematic Universe movie was shared on social media as part of this weekend's San Diego Comic-Con Málaga in Spain. It was an event that saw stars like Anthony Mackie, Winston Duke, and David Harbor make an appearance, with this latest look coming arriving as a little more than a high-res look at Robert Downey Jr.'s take on a classic comic book villain.

Doctor Doom takes center stage in the new Avengers: Doomsday poster. He's looking as menacing as ever, striking a pose similar to the one we've seen before but with somewhat better lighting. The real highlight from the new poster, however, is the three Latverian witches standing behind him.

These three witches – and their hidden identities – have been the subject of much debate amongst MCU fans the last few months. These same mystery characters brought their purple, red, and green robes to San Diego Comic-Con in California this past July. The average onlooker might assume these characters will be little more than henchmen to be discarded in a massive CGI fight sequence, but some aren't so convinced.

articles.title: Fourth RuneScape officially revealed
articles.summary: Jagex has revealed a fourth RuneScape MMO built in Unreal Engine, alongside an animated series made with YouTuber MoistCr1TiKaL.
body: After revealing the new game at RuneFest in Birmingham over the weekend, the developer also announced a new RuneScape animated adaptation, made in partnership with YouTuber Charlie "MoistCr1TiKaL" White, is also on the way.

According to the studio's own blurb, the game will "bring the world of Gielinor to life in Unreal Engine, combining the depth, freedom and community-led spirit that have defined RuneScape for 25 years with the technology and game design possibilities of today".
The new MMO, currently going by the working title RS4, is still in early development, with Jagex saying it's at least a few years from release and has yet to settle on an official name.

A numbered sequel might seem like the obvious name given RuneScape's history. The game was rebranded RuneScape 2 in 2004 and RuneScape 3 in 2013 before Jagex abandoned numbering altogether, folding everything back into a single live service. These days, the RuneScape stable also includes Old School RuneScape and spin-off RuneScape: Dragonwilds, both still active and separate from whatever RS4 eventually becomes.

articles.title: Inde Navarrette Teases X-Men Role, Says She's 'Doing Everything Humanly Possible' to Do Rogue Justice
articles.summary: Inde Navarrette has opened up about playing Rogue in X-Men, saying she's "doing everything humanly possible" to make sure she does the character justice. The Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) X-Men reboot movie has a lot to live up to.
body: The actress, who was picked to play the power-siphoning superhero earlier this year, told the LA Times that she's not taking her role in the reboot lightly. In fact, she's doing anything but.

"I'm doing everything humanly possible because I love that character," Navarrette said. "I've studied that character. I want to do it justice for myself, for [director Jake Schrieier], for what they want to portray and also for what I as a fan want her to be like. I’m doing everything, exclamation point."

Having parts in shows like 13 Reasons Why and Superman & Lois means Navarrette has been on TV screens for years, but her role as Nikki in low-budget horror phenomenon Obsession took her fame to a new level. Through all of the Oscar buzz and turned-down parts, it was Schreier's X-Men she decided to sign on to for one of her first post-Obsession roles.

Playing Rogue in X-Men means stepping into the shoes of a character with decades of history. Aside from the Mississippi-born mutant's history in comics, she's also already appeared in numerous animated and live-action projects, with actress Anna Paquin portraying her in films like the 2000 X-Men movie and X2: X-Men United.

videos.title: GT World Series 2026 | Round 3 - Singapore | Nations Cup [ENGLISH]
videos.summary: The 2026 World Series has now passed its halfway mark, with Round 3 taking place in Singapore.
body: In the previous Round in Tokyo, reigning champion José Serrano dominated the race right up until the final lap, only to drop to 5th place due to a costly penalty. This dramatic turn of events has significantly impacted the Points Ranking, in a race where the all the Spaniards were expected to hold the advantage.

Will current leader Kylian Drumont, fresh off his victory in the chaotic Round 2, build momentum to pull away from the pack? Will the Spanish drivers stage a comeback? Or will Valerio Gallo, who has been biding his time and closing in on the leaders, finally launch a serious charge?
With the World Finals fast approaching, the battle for the Nations Cup is becoming increasingly unpredictable. Witness how the competition unfolds!
